kjv: Ye shall not eat of every tree
mine: You must not eat from any tree
note: Hebrew lo' tokhlu mikkol 'ets means "you shall eat from no tree"; the KJV wording can be read as "not from all (only some) trees," which blunts the serpent's distortion.

Hebrew ke'lohim can be "like God" or "like gods/divine beings"; since 'elohim in the same verse is God, and 3:22 says "like one of us," either is possible, but the KJV chooses the plural. Context: like God (medium confidence). Elohim earlier in the verse is God, and the serpent promises a share in God's own knowledge; 3:22 'like one of us' confirms divine knowledge, though its plural leaves room for the heavenly council. The plural participle yod'e fits either reading. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV and CSB have 'like God'. Other possible meanings: (1) 'like gods' — LXX hos theoi, Vulgate sicut dii, KJV; (2) 'like divine beings', i.e. members of the heavenly council (cf. 3:22 'one of us') — NJPS, NET; (3) 'like great ones/princes' — Targum Onkelos, avoiding a direct comparison with God.

Hebrew hu' (masculine) refers to zera' "offspring"; the KJV's "it" treats the offspring collectively while "his heel" in the same verse is personal. The verb shuph is better "strike/crush" than "bruise." Traditionally read messianically.

kjv: cursed is the ground for thy sake
mine: cursed is the ground because of you
note: Hebrew ba'avurekha means "on account of you"; modern "for thy sake" suggests "for your benefit."
